_comment: Second real (non-dry) retraining run -- WBS 4.3.5, 2026-08-26, Colab T4.
Trained on the pool after folding in 9 new PHONE-SMS-INBOX export batches
(2026-07-25 through 2026-08-01), which grew the training pool 11,942 ->
18,938 unique (masked-text) rows. WBS 6.4.6's holdout set (carved out
2026-08-18, datasets/holdout/holdout.csv) was correctly excluded from this
pool -- see PIPELINE.md's 2026-08-26 entry on the build_dataset.py fix
that made this possible (it previously had no awareness of the holdout
carve-out and would have silently put those rows back into training).
Committed here rather than beside the checkpoint because ai/models/*/ is
git-ignored. The candidate weights (~1.1 GB) live only in Google Drive at
this manifest: same labeled dataset, same seed 42, same training code.

baseline_checkpoint._comment: The currently-deployed ai/models/xlm-roberta-smishing/ -- same baseline compared against in the 2026-08-17 run.

decision.reason: significantly better: 181 fixes vs 58 regressions (p=0.0000), macro-F1 0.9186 -> 0.9451

zero_reports_was_deliberate: Same as the 2026-08-17 run: no validated user reports exist yet, so
the manifest records 'null (no report store consulted)' rather than a
zero that could be misread as 'none were filed'.
why_the_baseline_score_dropped_from_0.95: This is the most important number to explain, not a red flag on the
deployed model. Every earlier measurement of the baseline -- 0.9438 in
AI_MODEL_RESULTS.md, 0.9520 in the 2026-08-17 run, 0.95 in the
2026-08-18 holdout confusion run -- was scored on a validation slice
drawn overwhelmingly from data the baseline had already trained on or
This run's validation slice is drawn from the pool AFTER folding in
~8,000 new raw-inbox rows the baseline has never seen at all (exported
training date). That is a genuinely harder, more honest test of the
deployed model's real-world generalization -- and its score fell to
0.9186 under it. The candidate, trained on that same new data, recovers
to 0.9451 -- notably higher than the baseline ever scored even on its
In plain terms: the deployed model is measurably worse at handling the
kinds of messages that have shown up since it was trained, and
retraining on that new data closes most of that gap.
what_drove_the_improvement: The 9 new PHONE-SMS-INBOX export files (2026-07-25 through 2026-08-01),
folded into the training pool this session -- see PIPELINE.md's
2026-08-26 entry for exactly which files and the row-count accounting.
Fix transitions skew heavily Spam->Ham (87) and Ham->Spam (67), meaning
most of the improvement is the candidate learning to tell honest
marketing/promo apart from personal/transactional messages more
reliably -- consistent with the new raw-inbox batch being real,
everyday phone traffic rather than curated corpus rows.
